title: OIDC attestor mints IAA2 identity from an unverified JWT payload
description:
EXPLOITABLE NOW. Full identity spoofing with no cryptography involved.

persona-attestors/src/oidc.rs:34-41 parse_jwt_payload() base64-decodes segment [1] of a JWT and returns it as trusted JSON. The signature segment is never read, let alone verified, and no issuer key is ever fetched or pinned. claim_from_jwt() (oidc.rs:61-93) then builds a Claim entirely out of that unverified payload:
  - sub  (oidc.rs:64) -> the SPIFFE ID path
  - iss  (oidc.rs:65) -> TrustDomain::OrgOidc, i.e. the trust domain authority
  - exp  (oidc.rs:66,75-79) -> IdentityAssurance::Iaa2 if exp > now, else Iaa1

TRIGGER: write a file at $HOME/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json containing {"id_token":"<b64url of {\"sub\":\"ceo@corp.example\",\"iss\":\"https://accounts.google.com\",\"exp\":9999999999}>.AAAA"} (any 3-part string; the signature bytes are never inspected). Same via $HOME/.azure/msal_token_cache.json -> IdToken.*.secret (oidc.rs:133-141) or accessTokens.json -> idToken (oidc.rs:145-152).

CONSEQUENCE: scan_token_caches() is called from enumerate() (oidc.rs:162-165), which is the path personad actually uses to issue credentials. persona-grpc/src/service.rs:120-137 selects the claim with the HIGHEST assurance across all attestors, so the forged Iaa2 claim beats every genuine Iaa1 claim (ssh, gpg, did:key). service.rs:178-185 then signs a real JWT-SVID for spiffe://accounts.google.com/user/ceo@corp.example/via/oidc-cached with identity_assurance "iaa2". Any relying party trusting personad now believes an attacker-chosen corporate identity, verified by a valid ES256 signature.

The file header ponytail comment ("manual JWT payload parsing without signature validation | upgrade to jsonwebtoken crate when validation is needed") frames this as deferred polish. It is not: enumerate() is the live issuance path, so unverified input directly determines both the subject and the assurance level of an issued credential. This is distinct from the known/tracked "prove() is unimplemented" gap.

Note the bar is low: any code running as the user can write those paths, and so can any tool that legitimately manages them. Minimum fix is to verify the signature against the issuer JWKS, or (if the no-network-IO constraint is to be kept) cap cache-derived claims at Iaa1 and stop deriving the trust domain from an unverified iss.
